subject: MSA + Order Form — auto-renew opt-out mechanics and notice window alignment
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@tidewater.health>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tidewater Procurement <procurement@tidewater.health>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — auto-renew / termination mechanics

Connor —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to send our redlines so legal can confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a mutual opt-out flow. Two items in particular:

1) Narrow the auto-renew window from 90 -> 60 days (Procurement prefers 60).
2) Add a mutual termination for convenience with a 60-day notice and limited transition support (we proposed a 60-day notice / 30-day ramp).

I've attached our marked-up MSA (Tidewater_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a PDF of our proposed order form language for the TFC clause. Can your team confirm whether those are acceptable or suggest alternative notice timing?

We'd like to keep the commercial timetable the same, so if we can resolve this quickly we'll move the order form to signature next week.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Director, Strategic Procurement
Tidewater Health
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: Tidewater_MSA_redline_v3.docx (MS Word redline), TW-0427_OrderForm_TerminationForConvenience.pdf (proposal)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@tidewater.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — auto-renew / termination mechanics

Lena —

Appreciate the redlines and the clear summary. I pulled Karthik (legal) and Mina (renewals lead) into the thread so we can coordinate quickly. High-level: the team generally supports the principle of mutual opt-out, but we need to reconcile two items before we can agree to the exact language you proposed:

- Operational impact of a 60-day notice paired with our dedicated capacity model (we need to confirm capacity unpinning and potential billing proration mechanics).
- How transition support (your 30-day ramp) maps to our SLA/exit obligations — specifically, what counts as "reasonable assistance" vs. billable professional services.

Karthik, can you review the attached and flag any legal non-starters? Mina, can you confirm whether we can support a 60-day runout operationally (vs our standard 90-day)? If we can't, what internal concession could we offer (e.g., shortened ramp, one-time credit, or limited support package)?

Lena — we'll come back with a short set of alternative options by EOD tomorrow so Procurement has something to review. If you'd prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute alignment call tomorrow at 11am PT.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — auto-renew / termination mechanics

Team —

I reviewed Tidewater's mark-up. Summary of legal posture + proposed concessions below (high level):

1) Auto-renew window: 90 -> 60 days is acceptable if we add a short operational notice carveout for customers in dedicated pools (we propose: "60 days except where Customer uses Dedicated Capacity; in such case, Redwood shall provide as much transition notice as operationally feasible and will offer a one-time capacity decommitment credit" ). This preserves predictability for us while giving Tidewater the 60-day commercial guarantee.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC): we cannot accept an unconstrained mutual TFC with no limitation on liability or return of pre-paid credits. Proposed compromise: mutual TFC with 60-day notice, Redwood provides transition assistance limited to two weeks of remote runbook support (included), plus the option to purchase a paid ramp package for additional onsite/engagement hours. Refunds for pre-paid usage should be prorated for unused full months only.

3) Carveouts and operational definitions: we should define "transition assistance" and "Decommit window" in the order form to avoid scope creep. I attached a short redline snippet with the alternative language for insertion (see attachment: redline_snippet.txt).

Next steps: Connor, send these alternatives to Tidewater and see whether they prefer the capacity carveout or a one-time financial concession (credit). Mina, please confirm the accounting/billing treatment for prorated refunds and whether Finance requires a minimum notice for capacity decommitments.

—Karthik
Assistant GC, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_snippet.txt (proposed alternate language)
From: Lena Park <lena.park@tidewater.health>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tidewater Procurement <procurement@tidewater.health>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — auto-renew / termination mechanics

Connor / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast review and the proposals. A couple of clarifications from Procurement:

- Tidewater wants predictable customer rights; the Dedicated Capacity carveout is acceptable so long as it is narrowly scoped and includes an explicit time-to-decommit estimate (we suggested 45 days as an estimate).
- For TFC refunds, procurement prefers pro-rata refunds at daily granularity for any pre-paid months where service is not delivered; if that is unacceptable we can accept monthly proration but we'll need a commercial credit to bridge the delta.

We can be flexible on transition support being limited to two weeks if Redwood is willing to commit to a paid ramp option at a fixed daily rate that Tidewater can elect up to 30 days post-notice. That gives Procurement predictability.

If Karthik can draft the exact carveout language with a 45-day decommit estimate and a defined paid ramp rate, Procurement will take that to internal counsel and (barring unexpected comments) we should be able to sign next week.

Lena
Director, Strategic Procurement
Tidewater Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2026 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: follow-ups and exec approval ask — Tidewater (TW-2026-0427)

Quick internal note before we send the draft back to Tidewater Monday morning:

- Offer summary to present: allow mutual TFC with 60-day notice; carve out Dedicated Capacity but commit to a 45-day "decommit estimate" in the order form; include two weeks of complimentary remote transition support and an optional paid ramp package (rate: $1,200/day) available to the customer up to 30 days after notice.
- Billing: Finance confirmed monthly proration only; Karthik recommended offering a one-time commercial credit equivalent to one week of average spend as a bridge if Tidewater insists on daily proration.
- Approval ask: can we greenlight the one-week credit (capped at $15k) for this deal to keep signature timelines? Mina — please confirm final numbers and that the credit can be recorded against the TW-0427 ARR bucket.

I'll draft final language (including the Dedicated Capacity carveout phrase Karthik proposed) and circulate for sign-off tonight. If we get alignment, we will send to Tidewater and ask for an internal counsel confirmation by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
